title: Marked Pedagogies: Examining Linguistic Biases in Personalized Automated Writing Feedback

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual prompting of student attributes ('does not meet academic standards' vs. 'exceeds academic standards') followed by log-odds ratio analysis (Marked Words framework) to identify distinctive lexical shifts in LLM-generated writing feedback.

Counterfactual prompting of student attributes ('English language learner' vs. no specification) followed by log-odds ratio analysis to measure pedagogical shifts toward grammar/mechanics vs. substantive feedback.

Counterfactual prompting of student attributes ('learning disability' vs. no specification) followed by log-odds ratio analysis to identify lexical shifts indicating lowered expectations and simplified vocabulary.

Counterfactual prompting using explicit racial/ethnic descriptors (Black, Hispanic, Asian vs. White) and racialized names, followed by log-odds ratio analysis to detect stereotype-aligned language and differential feedback focus.

Counterfactual prompting using explicit gender descriptors (Female vs. Male) and gendered names, followed by log-odds ratio analysis to detect differences in affective language, tone, and objective critique.

Counterfactual prompting of socio-psychological states ('unmotivated' vs. 'motivated') followed by log-odds ratio analysis to identify shifts in constructive criticism versus enthusiastic encouragement.
